newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds end higher on Bezeq sale.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds end higher on Bezeq sale.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Monday ahead of Tuesday's publication of the June consumer price index and on news of a deal to sell shares in Bezeq Israel Telecom, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.1 pct to 109.64
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.12 pct to 109.39
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.06 pct to 109.79
* Dollar-linked government bonds: -0.04 pct to 111.36
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 107.81
Volume including Makams was a low 128 million shekels.
"The market opened with good demand for most bonds, except dollar-linked bonds, which traded unchanged," said Ilan Doron of Solid Financial Markets.

Tiki Hadad of IBI Investment House said news that Merrill Lynch is buying shares equal to 12.5 percent of Bezeq was the main reason for higher bond price. Merrill Lynch will pay for $250 million to be transferred to the government next week.
"Because the government will be getting money from the sale it will need to raise less money in the debt market," she said.
Analysts said last-minute inflation forecasts were pointing to a relatively high June CPI.
"We believe the CPI will surprise us by being higher than expected -- around 0.7-0.8 percent against previous estimates of 0.6 percent immediately after the shekel depreciation," Doron said.
The shekel fell sharply against the dollar after the government instituted changes in the exchange rate mechanism and the Bank of Israel slashed interest rates on June 18.
Doron said that if June's CPI were on the high end of expectations, demand for CPI-linked bonds would rise.
He said unlinked bonds would already feel tomorrow the effect of upward revisions in the estimated CPI, even though the index is not released until the end of the day.
"Traders will sell unlinked bonds tomorrow and yields will rise slightly, but they will then stabilise around the new levels," Doron said.
He predicted that yields on the one-year Makam, now at 12.8 percent, would rise and gradually stabilise at the 12.9 percent to 13 percent.
Yields on CPI-linked bonds will continue to fall because of higher inflation in the coming months and because of the tight supply of bonds in the market, especially CPI-linked bonds, Doron said.

"In July the government will raise 1.6 billion shekels in the debt market against bond redemptions of 3.4 billion. In August the bond redemptions will be even higher, at 4.1 billion shekels," Doron said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.56 shekels)
